extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and USPTO filing staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and quality/formatting requirements for submitting correspondence, applications, petitions, and other papers to the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (addresses, identification, signatures, transmission methods, receipt dates, and petition evidence requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of specified mailing addresses (37 CFR 1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for correspondence submitted via the USPTO patent electronic filing system, all correspondence intended for the USPTO must be addressed to either 'Director of the United States Patent and Trademark Office, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, Virginia 22313-1450' or to specific areas within the Office provided in this section. When appropriate, correspondence should also be marked for the attention of a particular office or individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different addresses are specified for patent correspondence (Commissioner for Patents, P.O. Box 1450), Patent Trial and Appeal Board matters, Office of General Counsel, Office of Public Records (Assignment Recordation Services, Document Services), and Office of Enrollment and Discipline (Mail Stop OED). Improper correspondence to certain PO Boxes may not be filed elsewhere and may be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking correspondence for special mail stops and proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain correspondence (e.g., PCT-related letters, ex parte or inter partes reexamination correspondence, supplemental examination, patent term extension correspondence, maintenance fee payments) should be additionally marked with specified 'Mail Stop' identifiers (e.g., 'Mail Stop PCT', 'Mail Stop Ex Parte Reexam', 'Mail Stop Supplemental Examination', 'Mail Stop Maintenance Fee', 'Mail Stop Hatch-Waxman PTE').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appropriate, communications should also be marked to the attention of a particular individual. Use of the specific addresses and mail stop markings is strongly encouraged because it facilitates processing; some misaddressed mail may be returned or significantly delayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of correspondence (37 CFR 1.4(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence comprises (1) correspondence relating to services and facilities of the Office (general inquiries, publication requests, assignment transmissions, etc.) and (2) correspondence in and relating to a particular application or other proceeding in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different subparts govern filing/processing of national, international, reexamination, supplemental exam, extension of term, inter partes reexams, international design applications, and Board proceedings; file papers according to the appropriate subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each file must be complete in itself / duplicate copies (37 CFR 1.4(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A separate copy of every paper to be filed in a patent, patent file, or other proceeding must be furnished for each file to which the paper pertains, since each file must be complete in itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing duplicate copies of correspondence in the same file should be avoided except when the Office requires duplicate copies. The Office may dispose of duplicate copies in the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate papers for distinct subjects (37 CFR 1.4(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each distinct subject, inquiry, or order must be contained in a separate paper to avoid confusion and delay; subjects provided for on a single Office or WIPO form may be contained in a single paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph ¶ 5.01.01 'Separate Paper Required' is provided to notify applicants. USPTO may return or enter such combined papers but requires future compliance. Example: an affidavit, petition, or other distinct items must be separate. If applicant is pro se, include copy of the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handwritten signature requirement (37 CFR 1.4(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each piece of correspondence that requires a person's signature must be an original handwritten signature personally signed in permanent dark ink or be a direct/indirect copy (photocopy or facsimile) of an original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design patent practitioners must indicate their design status by placing the word 'design' adjacent to their handwritten signature. If a copy of an original is filed, the original should be retained as evidence; Office may require submission of the original if authenticity is questioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: S-signature format and requirements (37 CFR 1.4(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: An S-signature (signature between forward slashes) may be used instead of a handwritten signature for paper, facsimile, or USPTO electronic filing system attachments; it must consist only of letters and/or Arabic numerals with permitted punctuation and be enclosed by single forward slashes (e.g., /Dr. James T. Jones, Jr./).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patent practitioner signing pursuant to §1.33(b)(1) or (2) must supply their registration number as part of or adjacent to the S-signature; '#' may be used only when appearing before a practitioner's registration number. Design practitioners must indicate 'design' adjacent to the last slash. The signer's name should be printed/typed adjacent to the S-signature and be reasonably specific to recognize identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing signatures (37 CFR 1.4(d)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence submitted via the USPTO patent electronic filing system may be signed by a graphic representation of a handwritten signature or a graphic representation of an S-signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of graphic representations is permitted only when submitted via the USPTO patent electronic filing system in accordance with system requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications upon presentation of papers (37 CFR 1.4(d)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation (signing, filing, submitting, or later advocating) of any paper to the Office constitutes a certification under §11.18(b). Violations of §11.18(b)(2) can lead to sanctions under §11.18(c); practitioners may also face disciplinary action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certifications include certifying the paper presented and certifying that an inserted S-signature is the signer's own. Persons submitting documents signed by another must have reasonable basis to believe the signature was actually inserted by that person and should retain evidence of authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office forms: no changes to certification statements
rubrics_metrics.description: No changes to certification statements on Office forms (oath/declaration, terminal disclaimer, petition, nonpublication request, etc.) may be made. Existing text other than certification statements may be modified/deleted/added only if all text identifying the form as an Office form is removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation of an Office form with text identifying it as such constitutes a certification under §11.18(b) that the existing text and certifications have not been altered other than permitted EFS-Web customization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified documents and facsimile not acceptable for statutorily required certifications (37 CFR 1.4(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a document is required by statute to be certified, a copy (including photocopy or facsimile) of the certification is not acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certified documents must be originals where required by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of assistance when no registered practitioner of record (37 CFR 1.4(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who has not made of record a registered attorney or agent may be required to state whether assistance was received in the preparation or prosecution of the patent application for which any compensation was given, and if so, to disclose the name(s) of persons providing such assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assistance includes preparing specification, amendments, or other papers but excludes merely making drawings by draftsmen or typists doing stenographic services.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO may require ratification/confirmation/evidence of authenticity of signature (37 CFR 1.4(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may require ratification, confirmation (including submission of a duplicate with proper signature), or evidence of authenticity of a signature when there is reasonable doubt as to authenticity (e.g., signature variations or mismatch between signature and printed name).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office will request additional proof where signature authenticity is doubtful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification required on correspondence concerning an application (37 CFR 1.5(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: No correspondence relating to an application should be filed prior to receipt of the assigned application number; correspondence concerning a previously filed application must identify conspicuously on the top page the application number (series code and serial number), or the serial number and filing date, or international application/registration number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If correspondence lacks such identification it will be returned. Returned correspondence resubmitted within two weeks will be considered as received on the original date; applicants may use Certificate of Mailing/Transmission (§1.8) or Priority Mail Express (§1.10) for resubmissions if they desire the benefit of the deposit date. Correspondence should also state first-listed inventor name, title of invention, filing date, and if known, group art unit or examiner name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification requirements for letters concerning patents (37 CFR 1.5(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters about a patent (other than maintenance fee payments) should state the patent number and date of issue, the patentee's name, and the title of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For maintenance fee payment letters, see §1.366(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt date stamping rules (37 CFR 1.6(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence received in the USPTO is stamped with the date of receipt except in specified situations: the office is closed on weekends/holidays (no receipt), Priority Mail Express filings are stamped with USPS deposit date (§1.10), facsimile transmissions get date stamp when complete transmission received (except weekends/holidays), electronic filings receive a receipt date equal to Eastern Time when received (including weekends/holidays).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic filing via USPTO patent electronic filing system will be accorded a receipt date/time in Eastern Time regardless of weekend/holiday. New applications cannot be submitted by facsimile and are not entitled to Certificate of Transmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facsimile transmission rules and limitations (37 CFR 1.6(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence, including authorizations to charge a deposit account, may be transmitted by facsimile, with the receipt date being the date the complete transmission is received (subject to weekend/holiday exceptions). Each transmission session should be limited to correspondence to be filed in a single application or proceeding, and include the relevant application/control/interference/trial/patent number as part of sender identification on the fax cover sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facsimile transmissions are not permitted (and will not be accorded a date of receipt) for certain categories (see enumerated exceptions), and transmitting multiple applications in one session can impede processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories not entitled to facsimile submission (37 CFR 1.6(d) exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Facsimile transmissions are not permitted and will not be accorded a date of receipt for: certified documents specified in §1.4(f); documents that cannot receive benefit of certificates of mailing/transmission as specified in §1.8(a)(2); color drawings under specified sections; requests for reexamination (§1.510 or §1.913) or supplemental examination (§1.610); correspondence in applications subject to a secrecy order that are directly related to secrecy order content; and in contested cases and trials before the PTAB except as the Board expressly authorizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.6(d)(3)-(7) for detailed lists. Continued prosecution application under §1.53(d) may be transmitted to the Office by facsimile but is not entitled to Certificate of Transmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facsimile-transmitted continued prosecution application petition requirements (37 CFR 1.6(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office has no evidence of receipt of a continued prosecution application under §1.53(d) transmitted by facsimile, the transmitting party may petition the Director to accord a filing date as of the transmission date, provided the party (i) informs the Office promptly, (ii) supplies an additional copy, and (iii) includes a statement attesting to previous transmission and evidence such as the sending unit’s report or other evidence generated within one business day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may require additional evidence to determine if the application was transmitted/received on the date in question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing system receipt and petition rules (37 CFR 1.6(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence submitted via the USPTO patent electronic filing system will be accorded a receipt date equal to the Eastern Time when received; if the Office has no evidence of receipt of required national stage correspondence submitted via the system, the party may petition the Director to accord the national stage correspondence a receipt date as of the official submission date, subject to requirements (notification, additional copy, attestation, and acknowledgement receipt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must include prompt notice, additional copy, statement attesting prior submission, and a copy of the USPTO acknowledgment receipt or equivalent evidence. Office may require more evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: New applications cannot be faxed / Certificate of Transmission inapplicability
rubrics_metrics.description: New patent applications cannot be transmitted by facsimile and are not entitled to the benefit of a Certificate of Transmission under §1.8; a continued prosecution application under §1.53(d) may be transmitted by facsimile but is not entitled to Certificate of Transmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged to file new applications via the USPTO patent electronic filing system when permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Returned correspondence resubmission two-week rule (MPEP §502 / §1.5 guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any correspondence returned to the sender for lack of proper identification, if resubmitted within two weeks of the mail date on the cover letter, will be considered by the Office as received on the original date of receipt of the correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not resubmitted within two weeks, the resubmission's receipt date will be the date of receipt of the resubmission. Applicants may use Certificate of Mailing/Transmission (§1.8) or Priority Mail Express (§1.10) for resubmissions if they want the deposit date benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information to include on incoming papers to aid processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Incoming papers pertaining to a filed application should carry items to assist USPTO: (A) Application number (including series code), (B) Art Unit number (from most recent Office communication), (C) Filing date, (D) Name of the examiner who prepared the most recent Office action, (E) Title of invention, (F) Confirmation number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph ¶ 5.01 'Proper Heading for Incoming Papers' is provided as a reminder. Insufficient information causes difficulty matching incoming papers to application files and delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred online requests for certified/uncertified copies
rubrics_metrics.description: It is preferred that requests for certified or uncertified copies of patent and trademark documents be made online through the Certified Copy Center storefront at www.uspto.gov/CertifiedCopyCenter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper requests should be addressed to Mail Stop Document Services if mailed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate general mailing addresses and hand-delivery locations
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO maintains three separate general mailing addresses: for patent applications/patent-related papers (Commissioner for Patents, P.O. Box 1450), for trademark documents (Commissioner for Trademarks, P.O. Box 1451), and for other correspondence and certain recordation/document services (Director, P.O. Box 1450). Patent-related papers may be hand-carried to the Customer Service Window, Knox Building, 501 Dulany Street; trademark papers to the Trademark Assistance Center walk-up window at 600 Dulany Street.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correspondence cannot be hand-carried to Regional Offices. Use the correct address/mail stop for faster processing; use USPTO website or Official Gazette to confirm addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special mail stops and strict document type matching
rubrics_metrics.description: Special mail stops are established to forward particular types of correspondence quickly; only the specified document type for a mail stop should be placed in an envelope addressed to that mail stop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If documents other than the specified type are addressed to that department, they will be significantly delayed in reaching the appropriate area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid combining mixed-area correspondence in one envelope
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who correspond with the USPTO are strongly encouraged not to include correspondence which will have to be directed to different areas (e.g., Patents and Trademarks) of the Office in a single envelope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placing papers in separately addressed envelopes reduces likelihood of delay and unnecessary processing steps by USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Mail Express petitions: correct filing date discrepancy (37 CFR 1.10(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: When there's a discrepancy between the filing date accorded by the Office and the 'date accepted' entered by USPS on the Priority Mail Express label, a petition under §1.10(c) should be filed promptly and include showing that the Priority Mail Express label number was placed on each piece prior to mailing and a true copy of the label showing the 'date accepted' or other official USPS notation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt filing after becoming aware of the discrepancy is required; do not rely on late petitions or insufficient evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Mail Express petitions: incorrectly entered date-in (37 CFR 1.10(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: For petitions to correct an incorrectly entered 'date accepted' by USPS, the petition must be filed promptly, include proof the label number was placed on the pieces before mailing, and show the correspondence was deposited before the last scheduled pickup on the requested filing date. The showing must be corroborated by USPS evidence or evidence that came into being within one business day of deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable corroboration includes USPS Corporate Account Mailing Statement or contemporaneous logbook entries (with label number, application/file ID, place/date/time of deposit, depositor initials). Evidence created prior to deposit or more than one business day later is inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Mail Express petitions: correspondence never received (37 CFR 1.10(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where Priority Mail Express correspondence was deposited but never received by the Office, a petition should be filed promptly and include proof that the label number was placed on each piece, a true copy of the originally deposited correspondence showing the label number, any returned postcard receipt, a copy of the mailing label showing 'date accepted', and a signed statement by the depositor stating date/time of deposit and that accompanying copies are true copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.10(e) applies only where the entire correspondence was not delivered; it does not apply to disputes over contents of correspondence when Office records show some documents. The Office may require additional evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Mail Express petitions: additional evidence and limitations (37 CFR 1.10(f) & related)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may require additional evidence to determine whether correspondence was deposited as Priority Mail Express on the date in question. Provisions also clarify that correspondence actually received by the Office will not be denied a filing date simply because it lacked sufficient postage or proper addressing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions must be supported by reliable contemporaneous evidence; otherwise relief will be denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Mail Express petitions: returned due to postal interruption/emergency (37 CFR 1.10(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: If correspondence mailed as Priority Mail Express was returned by USPS due to an interruption or emergency in service, a petition may be filed promptly that includes proof label number was placed on the documents, original correspondence or copy showing label number, copy of mailing label showing 'date accepted', and a statement establishing original deposit and that the copy is a true copy. The Office may require USPS confirmation of the interruption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedure does not apply if USPS returned the mail for incomplete address or insufficient postage. It applies only to returns due to interruption/emergency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Mail Express petitions: refused due to postal interruption (37 CFR 1.10(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: If USPS refused correspondence because of an interruption/emergency in Priority Mail Express service, a prompt petition may be filed that includes proof label number was placed on the papers, original or copy showing label number, and a statement by the person who attempted to deposit establishing the attempt and that the document/copy is the original or true copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office may require additional evidence such as a USPS letter confirming refusal due to interruption. Procedure does not apply when refusal was for reasons other than interruption/emergency (e.g., incomplete address or insufficient payment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Mail Express petitions: unable to be deposited due to Director-designated interruption (37 CFR 1.10(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: When an attempt to file by Priority Mail Express was prevented by an interruption/emergency in service designated by the Director, a petition must be filed in a manner designated by the Director promptly, include original correspondence or copy, and include a statement establishing that the correspondence would have been deposited but for the designated interruption. The Director will provide guidance on filing manner and will publish notice on USPTO website and Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies only when the Director has designated the interruption/emergency and the Director's notice will give procedural guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition timeliness and evidentiary standards for Priority Mail Express petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions under §1.10(c)-(i) generally must be filed promptly after the filer becomes aware of the issue; evidence should show label numbers were affixed prior to mailing/deposit and be corroborated by USPS evidence or contemporaneous evidence created within one business day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence created prior to deposit or more than one business day later is inadequate for §1.10(d); logs created within one business day with required details are acceptable corroboration. Petitioners should not rely on late-created affidavits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of correspondence related to reexamination, supplemental examination, and Board proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence concerning ex parte reexamination, inter partes reexamination, supplemental examination, or proceedings before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board have specified marking or addressing requirements (e.g., additional 'Mail Stop' notations) and may be governed by other rules (see relevant CFR sections §1.1(a)(3) and §42.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address and marking these matters as specified facilitates processing and ensures correct file routing; facsimile and other transmission exceptions may apply for these proceedings.
